title: ALPR reason-entry compliance and enforcement records — the July 22, 2022 "MANDATORY REASON FOR ALPR QUERIES" memo
summary:
Built on the July 22, 2022 interoffice memorandum "MANDATORY REASON FOR ALPR QUERIES" produced 2026-06-23 under W012320-031126, which states that "inadequate entry of the REASON for your ALPR query will result in the suspension of your access to the databases and receipt of a Record of Discussion (ROD)," requires "Remedial training" for reinstated access, and — for queries run on behalf of outside agencies — states that "If there is no case or incident number, the query will not be completed." The same production included June 27, 2022 correspondence in which a Criminal Investigations Bureau sergeant conducting "an ALPR audit per department policy" recorded that a reason of "INVESTIGATION" "does not meet the requirement."

The request states, from the audit records produced under W012541-041426 and W012818-053026, that 105,315 queries were logged January 1, 2023 – August 31, 2026 and at least 64,891 (~62%) state "investigation" as the entire reason, median networkCount 112.

Records requested, June 1, 2022 to present:

- Item 1: the issued/signed version of the memo, including any version addressed to dispatchers.
- Item 2: the "Two previous memos" it references and records of the "in person lineup training" it describes.
- Item 3: Records of Discussion issued for inadequate REASON entry, per-year counts, and — if a ROD does not follow every inadequate entry — records describing the standard applied. Names eight specific query IDs from the W012541 audit records (2023-12-20 through 2026-02-25, networkCount 380–909) and asks for the ROD/suspension/remedial-training disposition of each, plus any log, index, or compilation tracking which queries resulted in a ROD, suspension, or training.
- Item 4: suspension and reinstatement records, including Flock and Vigilant user-account administration records, and per-year suspension counts.
- Item 5: remedial-training curricula, rosters, and completion records.
- Item 6: the ALPR audit described in the June 27, 2022 correspondence — query set reviewed, entries identified as deficient, responses received, determinations.
- Item 7: any review, audit, or monitoring of REASON entry conducted after July 22, 2022, with query sets, findings, and corrective actions.
- Item 8: ALPR Committee membership and charter, its meeting records, and records of the "Leadership meeting" and "CS meeting" at which the course of action for inadequate REASON entries was discussed.
- Item 9: audit records for the Vigilant search platform, which the memo identifies alongside Flock as subject to the audit that prompted it.

policy_promises.policy: SMPD interoffice memorandum, 2022-07-22 — "MANDATORY REASON FOR ALPR QUERIES"
policy_promises.quote: inadequate entry of the REASON for your ALPR query will result in the suspension of your access to the databases and receipt of a Record of Discussion (ROD)
policy_promises.tests: Whether any ROD, access suspension, or remedial training ever followed an inadequate REASON entry — against ~64,891 produced queries stating "investigation" as the entire reason.

policy_promises.quote: If there is no case or incident number, the query will not be completed.
policy_promises.tests: Whether queries lacking a case or incident number were nonetheless completed, and whether any record shows the stated refusal being applied.
The Department itself ruled a bare "INVESTIGATION" reason non-compliant in 2022; item 7 asks what review, if any, continued after the memo issued.

policy_promises.quote: agency must notify requester within 10 calendar days whether it will produce records

prior_pra_refs.note: Produced the July 22, 2022 memorandum and the June 27, 2022 audit correspondence on 2026-06-23; this request seeks the enforcement records those documents promise.
Source of the audit records the request quantifies and of the eight query IDs named in item 3.
Second tranche of search audit records making up the 105,315-query, Jan 2023–Aug 2026 span cited in the request.

filed_because: The Department set its own written standard for ALPR query reasons in 2022 — a case or incident number, with suspension and a Record of Discussion for inadequate entry — and separately ruled a bare "INVESTIGATION" reason non-compliant. Its own produced audit records show ~62% of queries over three and a half years stating exactly that. Either the enforcement records exist, or the answer is that a written suspension-and-discipline standard went unapplied across tens of thousands of queries. Asking for the RODs, suspensions, and training records puts that on the record either way.
notes:
Filed 2026-09-08; 10-day statutory determination due 2026-09-18.

Item 3 names eight specific query IDs as examples without limiting scope, so a per-query answer and a compilation-level answer are both requested. Item 9 extends the ask to Vigilant, which the 2022 memo names alongside Flock.
